full_failure_first.log: migration/patches/T10/T10-B1-bootstrap-failure-excerpt.txt (excerpt of the -v run; the whole output is in the task directory)
full_failure_first.error: Expected nil, but got: &fs.PathError{Op:"stat", Path:"../../configs", Err:0x2} at bootstrap_test.go:30, after cobra printed the usage block
why_this_is_a_fixture_problem_and_not_a_: the path comes from the default of the package-level CommandFlags (flag.go: Conf "../../configs"), i.e. a layout default aimed at the upstream repository's own example tree; the test never overrode it, so RunApp fails on the first step regardless of anything production-side

even with a config present, bootstrap() ends in kratos.App.Run(), which blocks on signal.Notify(os.Interrupt, ...) until Stop is called; the old test had no way to stop it, so it could only ever pass by erroring out early
the cobra root also inherits the arguments of the test binary when SetArgs is never called, which is the classic go-test leak this fixture now closes

what_the_fix_does: keeps the test name and the original semantics: build a Context with AppId and Version, call RunApp through the real path, require a nil return

uses the existing RunApp option to call root.SetArgs with --conf pointing at a temporary minimal config (env: unittest) plus --env and --daemon=false, so no user configuration and no remote config source is read

supplies a lifecycle test server implementing transport.Server: Start records that it ran and closes a channel, and a goroutine waiting on that channel calls the app's own Stop, so the run ends without sleeping, guessing timing, or sending a signal to the process

asserts the original meaning rather than an error string: the version reaches the app, the name is the Project + "/" + AppId composition that NewApp performs, the server started, the server was stopped through Stop, and the cleanup function returned by initApp ran

runs that whole path in a child test binary, because bootstrap fills package-level state no test can reset: the parsed-config singleton in bConfig (an init sync.Once plus a proto scanned in place) and the command flags bound to the root command. The parent process keeps its own state, and the child's own assertions plus its PASS line are checked by the parent
pinned_cobra_detail: spf13/cobra v1.10.2 declares SetArgs(a []string) with no result, and its pflag parses the single-dash '-conf' as the shorthand cluster -c with value 'onf'; the first attempt therefore failed with 'stat onf'. The test passes the long-form flags instead. This is a property of how upstream names its flags, and nothing in production was changed to accommodate it.
production_untouched: git status shows exactly one modified file, the _test.go file; bootstrap.go, cli.go, context.go, flag.go, options.go, types.go, daemon.go, app_info.go, process_unix.go and process_windows.go are unchanged by this step
